haiku-low.q1: Its document is deleted from the search index. An update to archived (or draft) becomes a delete by id with a version, so the product leaves search.
haiku-low.q2: The older change is rejected as a version conflict. It counts as stale, increments stale_skipped, is treated as done, and the newer document stays.
haiku-low.q3: That partition stops and retries only the failed items, with backoff from 1 s doubling to a 60 s cap, with no retry limit and no skipping ahead. Offsets are not committed and an SLO alert fires.
haiku-low.q4: It goes to catalog.products.dlq with error, index and partition/offset, and an alert is raised. It is treated as done, so the older document stays and the product is not updated.
haiku-low.q5: At 50 GB ops drop search_slot, so changes since then never reach the topic. The slot is recreated and streaming restarts from now. Search keeps serving the current index with gaps; the only way back is a full rebuild.
haiku-low.q6: The alias products moves to the new index in one atomic call, only after the gate passes: lag under 5 s and document count within 0.5% of the active row count. The gate is rechecked every minute.
haiku-low.q7: In Kafka consumer group offsets, one group per index. An offset is committed only after the index acknowledges the batch writes, as last batch offset plus one.
haiku-low.q8: It resumes from the last committed offset and replays in order. Versions make replays stale or idempotent, though a product may briefly reappear if the store already purged its delete tombstone.
haiku-low.q9: Start offsets are recorded before S_low, and S_low before the snapshot. The v4 stream replays from those offsets after backfill, and later changes overwrite snapshot rows in commit order per id, so none are lost.
haiku-low.q10: Every row copied by the bulk backfill carries version = S_low, the LSN recorded before the snapshot opened.
haiku-low.q11: For 48 hours both consumer groups keep writing, so v3 gets every change. Rollback is one atomic alias move back to v3. After 48 hours with no rollback, the v3 group is stopped and products_v3 is deleted.
haiku-low.q12: Queries keep hitting products_v3 because the alias is untouched. A copy failure pauses backfill and resumes from the last acked id in a new snapshot. An abandoned rebuild deletes products_v4 and its group, with no effect on search.

sonnet.q1: It is deleted from the index (delete by id with the version, same new-must-be-at-least-stored rule). A not-found result counts as success.
sonnet.q2: The write hits a version conflict (older commit_lsn than stored), which is treated as stale. It increments stale_skipped and counts as done. The newer change stays.
sonnet.q3: It keeps that partition paused and retries only the failed items with backoff of 1 s, 2 s, 4 s, capped at 60 s, with no retry limit. It never skips ahead, doesn't commit offsets, lag grows and an SLO alert fires.
sonnet.q4: The event, error, index and partition/offset are produced to catalog.products.dlq, an alert is raised, and the change is treated as done. The older document stays. After a fix, the DLQ is redriven through the indexer, and versions stop it overwriting newer changes. If the DLQ produce fails, it goes to retry.
sonnet.q5: Ops drop search_slot to protect the primary, so changes since the drop never reach the topic. Search keeps serving the current index, now with gaps. Recovery: recreate the slot, restart the connector streaming from now, and do a full rebuild into a new index.
sonnet.q6: One atomic alias call removes products from the old index (v3) and adds it to the new one (v4). Before that, the backfill must be complete and acknowledged, the v4 consumer group started and caught up, refresh 1 s and replicas restored with green health, and the gate must pass: v4 lag under 5 s and v4 doc count within 0.5% of the active row count.
sonnet.q7: In Kafka consumer group offsets, one group per index (search-indexer-INDEX). The offset is committed (last batch offset + 1) only after every item in the batch is acknowledged or resolved by the index.
sonnet.q8: It resumes from the last committed offset and replays in order. Versions make the replayed writes stale or idempotent. A product can briefly reappear before its delete is replayed if the store has already purged the delete tombstone.
sonnet.q9: The end offsets of all 12 partitions are recorded first, then S_low, then the snapshot opens. After the backfill is fully acknowledged, the v4 consumer group starts at the recorded start offsets and replays. Changes older than S_low are stale against snapshot rows. Changes from S_low onward overwrite in commit order per id, so the last write is the latest committed state. Deleted rows are removed by the replayed delete.
sonnet.q10: version = S_low, the recorded pg_current_wal_lsn, for every row.
sonnet.q11: The v3 consumer group keeps running during a 48 h fallback window, so v3 still gets every change. Switching back is one atomic alias call to v3 and loses nothing. It ends when 48 h pass with no rollback. Then the v3 consumer group is stopped and deleted and products_v3 is deleted.
sonnet.q12: Nothing changes for search. The alias stays on products_v3 and every query goes to it. If the rebuild is abandoned, delete products_v4 and its consumer group. If the snapshot is lost mid-backfill, the backfill pauses and resumes from the last acknowledged id in a new snapshot. The doc does not say more about a failure during catch-up beyond the alias not moving until the gate passes.
